description:
From docs/perl-suite-audit-s392.md §2.  Every one of these dies at transpile
with a `Parser2 TODO:`-class refusal, which is a compiler GAP, not a blessed
non-support — so each needs a fix or a task, never a not-supported.md entry.

=== DONE s393d (a296b41) — family F-A1, 96% of the whole loss ===
`my @raw, @upgraded, @utf8;` — the comma-list `my`.  Parser2 already had the
branch for the SCALAR spelling (perl declares ONLY the first name and
evaluates the rest as a void expression, so the others are PACKAGE variables);
it tested `/^\$\w+$/`.  Widened to all three sigils, binding through the
existing `_fresh_container`.  opbasic/cmp.t TRANSPILE-FAIL -> 12078 ok /
0 not-ok, its pre-flip value to the digit; snapshot row spliced (s393e).

The 10-shape probe found the family's SECOND half, and it is now fixed too:
`_collect_lexical_names` had no case for the shape, so its conservative
fallback took EVERY symbol as declared and a named sub reading a TAIL name
refused with "file lexical captured by sub" — for a package global.  That was
wrong for the scalar spelling since it shipped.  Both consumers now call ONE
predicate, `_lead_decl_with_expr_tail` (Parser2.pm).  Guard:
Pl/t/my-decl-tail-01.t, 10 rows, 14 s, every expectation probed vs live perl.

MEASURED: corpus-diff IDENTICAL (the spelling occurs nowhere in perl-tests/ —
companion-suite only), gate 139/5148, full sweep GATE clean TOTAL 18535 (+3,
unchanged).  The other 17 TRANSPILE files were re-run in the same tree and are
UNMOVED, so F-A1 really was one file.

=== REMAINING — six families, 17 files, re-measured s393 ===
| family | refusal text | files |
|---|---|---|
| F-A2 attributed `my` | `unsupported declaration: my ($cows, @go, %bong) : teapots = …` | op/attrs.t, uni/attrs.t |
| F-B `our` non-assign | `unsupported our declaration: our $count++;` / `our \$TODO = \$::TODO;` | op/inccode.t, op/repeat.t, re/opt.t |
| F-C foreach head | `foreach without list` | op/const-optree.t, op/for-many.t |
| F-D my spans package | `my-lexical 'X' spans a package boundary` | io/shm.t, op/svleak.t, op/taint.t |
| F-E our shadows my | `our '$y' shadows a my-lexical` | comp/our.t |
| F-F state | `state $classcount in named sub (string eval)`; `non-scalar state declaration outside a named-sub statement: @a` | op/coresubs.t, op/lvref.t, op/decl-refs.t (already DIFF at 42) |
| singles | `Failed to compile s///e expression '"${\<<END}"` | base/lex.t |
| | `compound 'try'` | op/try.t |
| | `self-referential init: my %base_opts = ( … )` | run/runenv.t |
| | `lexical 'x__file__2' possibly captured by nested sub` | op/lexsub.t |
| | `Handle single node of unknown type: ref='PPI::Token::Operator'` | re/pat_rt_report.t |

Not part of this task: op/for.t (upstream PPI lexer bug, #253) and
re/reg_eval_scope.t (#269, parked behind #196).

METHOD THAT WORKED for F-A1 and should be repeated: find the SIBLING shape the
compiler already handles, widen ONE predicate rather than adding a branch, then
probe ~10 shapes against live perl — the probe is what found the second
consumer that disagreed.  Bar per family: corpus-diff + gate + full sweep
(TOTAL/LOST), then re-measure the family's files and splice their snapshot rows
with the cause in the header.
=== DONE s395a (44cc113) â family F-B, `our NAMES <non-assignment tail>` ===
`our $count++;`.  Same shape as F-A1's `my VAR <tail>`: declare the cell, then
lower `NAMES <tail>` through the ordinary expression machinery.  The gate in
_lower_our_decl demanded an ASSIGNMENT operator; it now asks only that the tail
start with an operator, and _tail_decl_convertible (the one consumer that cared,
for eval-tail position) widened with it.  Ten shapes probed vs perl.
  op/repeat.t   TRANSPILE-FAIL -> 47 ok / 3 not-ok
  op/inccode.t  TRANSPILE-FAIL -> COMPILES, dies at test 2 on coderef-in-@INC,
                which is that file's entire subject -> task #321
parser2-02.t's INVERSE row (`our $x, $y` must be refused) was an expectation
pinning a divergence; REWRITTEN with four stronger rows.  Guard: 3 run rows in
Pl/t/my-decl-tail-01.t.

=== DONE s395b (7c18251) â family F-A2, attributed declarations ===
Attributes are STRIPPED in one document pre-pass (_strip_typed_lexical_classes
became _strip_decl_decorations) and the drop is ANNOUNCED once per attribute per
file.  The probe found a live SILENT WRONG: PPI spells the attribute as
Operator(':') + Words inside a Statement::Variable, so `my $x : shared = 1;`
matched _lead_decl_with_expr_tail and printed EMPTY where perl prints 1.
  op/attrs.t   TRANSPILE-FAIL -> 28 ok / 61 not-ok
  uni/attrs.t  TRANSPILE-FAIL ->  8 ok / 26 not-ok
The remainder is the attribute PROTOCOL (MODIFY_*_ATTRIBUTES dispatch, the
compile error for an unconsumed attribute, attributes::get) -> task #322, with
a docs/not-supported.md entry that #322 DELETES rather than rephrases.

=== DONE s395c (0a6514d) â the single that was worth 2431 rows ===
re/pat_rt_report.t: `qr/A@{+}B/`.  `@{+}` is the VARIABLE @+ (perl's `${ NAME }`
takes a punctuation name).  ONE decision function, two consumers.  `$#-`/`$#+`
(one Magic token, not an ArrayIndex) were the second half.
  re/pat_rt_report.t  TRANSPILE-FAIL -> 2431 ok / 39 not-ok
It now reaches the `(?{ CODE })` block and blows the control stack -> task #324
(~82 more rows).

=== REMAINING after s395 ===
| family | files | note |
|---|---|---|
| F-C part 1: `for my ($q,$r) (LIST)` | op/for-many.t (71) | perl 5.36 n-at-a-time foreach.  A REAL FEATURE, not a parse gap: the loop vars ALIAS the list elements (the file's last tests mutate @array through them), so it needs the #267 splitter machinery k at a time. |
| F-C part 2: `for \%_ (@tests)` | op/const-optree.t (148) | NOT the same family â this is REFALIASING, see below. |
| F-D my spans package | io/shm.t (21), op/svleak.t (156), op/taint.t (0) | the _rename_spanning_lexicals decline; deep machinery (#291/#296 family), instrument before touching |
| F-E our shadows my | comp/our.t (7) | tiny population |
| F-F state | op/coresubs.t (1109) | `state $classcount` blocked by _shadow_rename_blocker = "string eval".  NB the file also needs B::walkoptree, so the reachable row count is unknown â MEASURE what it does after the state fix before sizing. |
| REFALIASING (new grouping) | re/opt.t (639), op/const-optree.t (148), op/lvref.t (199), op/decl-refs.t (402, at 42) | `our \$TODO = \$::TODO`, `for \%_ (@list)`, `\state @a = [...]`.  In PCL's model a scalar IS a box, so aliasing = sharing the box object, and a container alias = sharing the vector/hash â implementable.  ~1400 rows across four files; size it as its own task. |
| single: base/lex.t (120) | `Failed to compile s///e expression '"${\<<END}"` â heredoc inside `${\ }` inside s///e |
| single: op/try.t (28) | `compound 'try'` |
| single: op/lexsub.t (156) | dies in Pl/Parser.pm "Negative repeat count does nothing" |
| single: run/runenv.t (106) | BLOCKED ON #318, do not hack: `my %base_opts = (...), my ($out,$err) = ...;` (line 246 ends in a COMMA).  Probed: perl reads the PACKAGE %base_opts in the tail â `perl -e 'my %h=(a=>1), my ($x)=(join",",%h); print "[$x]"'` prints `[]`.  So the refusal is a false positive of the self-ref TEXT scan, but lifting it without #318 makes PCL read the FRESH hash and diverge the other way. |

=== F-D DIAGNOSED s395 (not fixed) â do not re-derive ===
`PCL_SPAN_DEBUG=1 ./pl2cl <file>` prints the rename pass's own refusal reason.
All three F-D files refuse at the SAME line (Pl/Parser2.pm ~2937,
`!(@sdecls == 1 && $dc == 1)`):

  op/taint.t   SPANREFUSE old_env_path@seg0: sdecls=0 dc=1
  io/shm.t     SPANREFUSE fetch@seg0: sdecls=0 dc=1   (+ store, same)
  op/svleak.t  SPANREFUSE a@seg0: sdecls=0 dc=0

and the sources say why:

  taint.t:34   my ($old_env_path, $old_env_dcl_path, $old_env_term);
  shm.t:83     my ($fetch, $store) = (0, 0);
  svleak.t:67  my @a;

`_scan_lex_facts` fills `scalar_decl{bare}` ONLY from `_single_scalar_decl`
(Pl/Parser2.pm:2578) -- i.e. `my $x` and `my $x = ...`.  So:

  (a) a LIST-form declaration (`my ($a, $b);`) registers NO scalar_decl for
      either name, hence sdecls=0 -> refuse -> the checker dies.  That is
      taint.t and shm.t.
  (b) a CONTAINER declaration (`my @a;`) is not on this path at all: both
      sdecls and _hard_decl_count ask about the '$' sigil, so dc=0 too.  That
      is svleak.t.

So F-D is one gap with two shapes, and neither is about the SPAN logic --
it is about which declaration forms the facts scan records.  Size the fix as
"record list-form and container declarations in the same facts", then re-check
what the rewrite loops below the refusal assume about the shape they got.
Both halves need the s372 two-population gate-SET measurement (this pass turns
refusals into rewrites, so the gate set moves in both directions).

=== s396 MEASUREMENTS â two of the remaining families are NOT reachable ===

F-C part 2 (refaliasing) DONE: tasks #325/#327 shipped it.  op/const-optree.t
TRANSPILE-FAIL -> 86 ok / 62; the 62 are optree-INSPECTION rows (B:: sub
inlinability, :method attributes), not aliasing.  re/opt.t transpiles now and
dies on re::optimization -> registered XDIFF (not-supported entry).

F-F op/coresubs.t (1109 rows) is UNREACHABLE, measured, do not size it again.
The state blocker was waived experimentally (pass eval_ok to
_shadow_rename_blocker at the named-sub state site) purely to measure: the file
then TRANSPILES and gets ZERO rows, crashing on
  Can't locate loadable object for module this module in @INC
which is `use B`.  Its whole method is op_list() = B::walkoptree over
B::svref_2object(...)->ROOT, comparing the OPTREE of CORE::word against a
user sub.  PCL has no perl optree, so this is the same class as
re::optimization.  The waiver was REVERTED (it would let a state rename hide a
cell from string eval, which is what the refusal exists to prevent).

F-E comp/our.t (7 rows): ATTEMPTED AND REVERTED -> task #328 with the eight
probe shapes.  Narrowing the refusal makes the file 7/7 but is a SILENT WRONG
(a use after `our $y` keeps reading the `my $y` it shadows), and the obvious
fix does not work: `main::$z` and `$z` are THE SAME CL SYMBOL, so qualifying
cannot escape a lexical binding.  Needs a global-read FORM.

STILL OPEN AND REACHABLE: F-D (io/shm.t 21, op/svleak.t 156, op/taint.t 0) and
F-C part 1 (op/for-many.t 71, needs #267's splitter k at a time).

=== s399: F-D SCALAR HALF DONE; the container half is TWO different things ===

FIXED (s399e): the LIST-form declaration.  `_scan_lex_facts` fills scalar_decl
only from _single_scalar_decl, so the span pass found no statement to rename
for `my ($fetch, $store) = (0, 0);` -> `sdecls=0 dc=1` -> refuse -> the CHECKER
killed the file.  perl declares each name of a list form exactly as the single
form does, and the pass renames ONE symbol inside the declaring statement
either way, so the two facts are merged for that pass in ONE accessor
(_scalar_decl_stmts = scalar_decl + the $-sigil entries of mlist_decl, which
already recorded exactly this for the capture-promotion pass).  The promotion
pass keeps reading the two facts separately -- merging there would process a
list decl twice.

  io/shm.t   TRANSPILE-FAIL -> TRANSPILES (rc 0)
  op/taint.t moves PAST the span refusal to two OTHER pre-existing refusals
             ("Failed to compile s///e expression", and the F6 oversized
             top-level form at 93,715 chars) -- still refused, new cause.

MEASURED: two-population GATE-SET scan (638 files: 111 perl-tests + 527 of
perl's t/ default dirs, op/cond.t excluded as always) before vs after -- FOUR
rows differ and only four: io/shm.t refusal -> OK, and three message-text-only
changes from the diagnostic below.  corpus-diff IDENTICAL over 111 files.
Guard: transpile-test-09.t "list-form my whose name spans a package boundary"
(3 inverse shapes in the same snippet).

DIAGNOSTIC (same commit): the checker's die now names the CANONICAL variable --
"my-lexical 'a' (canon @a) spans a package boundary".  It cost this session a
probe to learn that op/svleak.t dies on @a and not on $a, which the bare name
hid; op/goto.t is the third file the scan showed carrying it (canon $count).

NOT FIXED, and the s395 diagnosis (b) was imprecise -- the container half is
TWO distinct causes, neither of them "container decls are not recorded"
(container_decl HAS existed since W10-ext-3, with its own span loop):

  (b1) op/svleak.t dies on canon @a, and the container loop refuses because
       `canon_decl_count{@a} == 3` -- the file declares `my @a` three times
       (lines 67, 147 `tie my @a`, 174).  The file-uniqueness rule is
       deliberate ("a nested `let @x` under the defvar'd special is poison");
       lifting it is a direction-D question, not a facts-scan one.
  (b2) a CONTAINER NAME INSIDE a list decl (`my ($x, @rest) = (1,2,3);`
       spanning) still refuses.  mlist_decl already carries the pair the
       container loop wants, but that loop marks the decl via
       _file_lex_renamed and the DECL LOWERING has only a no-init
       SINGLE-container branch (_lower_block) -- so feeding it a list decl
       needs the lowering half too.  Probed s399: perl prints `1:2 3`, PCL
       refuses.  Occurs in NO measured file.

Both are on task #338.  With the scalar half done, F-D's reachable population
is exhausted: shm.t's 21 rows still hit IPC::SysV, svleak.t XS::APItest,
taint.t -T -- the s396 measurement stands.
